sub_criteria.name: agentic search design
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates an LLM-driven system that searches scholarly literature through more than one query: query reformulation, citation-graph traversal, iterative crawling, planning or tool use.

sub_criteria.name: baseline recall
sub_criteria.text: Reports what plain single-query or conventional keyword/dense database search recovers, as a measured baseline or ceiling that other systems are compared against.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Introduces or analyses an evaluation set for literature search, deep research or scholarly QA, and says how the set was built, annotated or scored.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval and reranking
sub_criteria.text: Contributes or evaluates the underlying retrieval or reranking method — dense/sparse retrieval, LLM rerankers, citation-graph or hybrid retrieval — on scientific documents.

sub_criteria.name: gains that fail
sub_criteria.text: Reports a failure to replicate, benchmark leakage or construction that inflates scores, a weak or unfairly tuned baseline, or a setting where the simple baseline is not beaten.

items.abstract_600: Transformer architectures have achieved state-of-the-art performance across natural language tasks, yet they fundamentally misrepresent the hierarchical nature of human language by processing text as flat token sequences. This results in quadratic computational cost, weak computational cost, weak compositional generalization, and inadequate discourse-level modeling. items.abstract_600: Large language model (LLM)-based agents that reason, plan, and act through tools, memory, and structured interaction are emerging as a promising paradigm for automating complex workflows. Recent systems such as OpenClaw and Claude Code exemplify a broader shift from passive response generation to action-oriented task execution. items.title: FinAbstain: Uncertainty-Calibrated Multimodal RAG for Selective Financial Forecasting
items.abstract_600: Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize financial narratives but may express high confidence when evidence is sparse, stale, or contradictory. This failure is especially consequential in forecasting, where filings, news, prices, volume, and technical signals can disagree. We present FinAbstain, a research framework for uncertainty-calibrated multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with selective prediction. items.title: WisPaper: Your AI Scholar Search Engine
items.abstract_600: We present \textsc{WisPaper}, an end-to-end agent system that transforms how researchers discover, organize, and track academic literature. items.title: Characterizing Deep Research: A Benchmark and Formal Definition
items.abstract_600: Information tasks such as writing surveys or analytical reports require complex search and reasoning, and have recently been grouped under the umbrella of \textit{deep research} -- a term also adopted by recent models targeting these capabilities. Despite growing interest, the scope of the deep research task remains underdefined and its distinction from other reasoning-intensive problems is poorly understood. items.abstract_600: The field of expert finding has seen a large number of approaches proposed both in universities and in industries, using a variety of new techniques in relevant data fields. items.abstract_600: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant strides across various information retrieval tasks, particularly as rerankers, owing to their strong generalization and knowledgetransfer capabilities acquired from extensive pretraining. items.title: Agent Laboratory: Using LLM Agents as Research Assistants
items.abstract_600: Historically, scientific discovery has been a lengthy and costly process, demanding substantial time and resources from initial conception to final results. To accelerate scientific discovery, reduce research costs, and improve research quality, we introduce Agent Laboratory, an autonomous LLM-based framework capable of completing the entire research process. items.abstract_600: Advancements in model algorithms, the growth of foundational models, and access to high-quality datasets have propelled the evolution of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC). Despite its notable successes, AIGC still faces hurdles such as updating knowledge, handling long-tail data, mitigating data leakage, and managing high training and inference costs. items.abstract_600: Introduction: Higher education institutions face persistent challenges of student retention and academic progress. Personalized adaptive learning has the potential to address these issues as it leverages educational technology to tailor learning pathways according to individual student needs. items.abstract_600: The evaluation of Deep Research Agents is a critical challenge, as conventional outcome-based metrics fail to capture the nuances of their complex reasoning. Current evaluation faces two primary challenges: 1) a reliance on singular metrics like Pass@1, creating a ''high-score illusion'' that ignores the quality, efficiency, and soundness of the reasoning process; and 2) the failure of static benchmarks to quantify crucial attributes like robustness and latent capability. items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for News Summarization
items.abstract_600: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automatic summarization but the reasons behind their successes are poorly understood. By conducting a human evaluation on ten LLMs across different pretraining methods, prompts, and model scales, we make two important observations. First, we find instruction tuning, not model size, is the key to the LLM’s zero-shot summarization capability. items.title: Minos: A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework for Provenance-Based Backward Tracking
items.abstract_600: Sophisticated cyber attacks, particularly Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs), require effective post-intrusion forensic analysis. items.title: Layer-wise Token Compression for Efficient Document Reranking
items.abstract_600: Transformer-based document cross-encoder rerankers are a central component of modern information retrieval systems. Despite their success, these models suffer from high computational costs due to processing long query-document sequences at inference time. A known approach to improve efficiency is token compression, which consists of aggregating groups of tokens together in the initial embedding layer, reducing the effective number of tokens, and making the computation faster. items.abstract_600: A previous study employing fMRI measures of retrieval-related neural selectivity reported that young, but not older, adults employ ‘retrieval gating’ to attenuate aspects of an episodic memory that are irrelevant to the retrieval goal. items.title: SeekerGym: A Benchmark for Reliable Information Seeking
items.abstract_600: Despite their substantial successes, AI agents continue to face fundamental challenges in terms of trustworthiness. Consider deep research agents, tasked with searching for information relevant to a given topic-while AI agents can perform effective information retrieval, there is little guarantee regarding the completeness of this information. Gaps in retrieved information can leave biases that mislead users even if the information they are given is correct and relevant. items.abstract_600: We present an open deep research system for long-form question answering, selected as a winning system in the text-to-text track of the MMU-RAG competition at NeurIPS 2025. items.title: DeepShop: A Benchmark for Deep Research Shopping Agents
items.abstract_600: Web agents for online shopping have shown great promise in automating user interactions across e-commerce platforms. Benchmarks for assessing such agents do not reflect the complexity of real-world shopping scenarios, as they often consist of overly simple queries with deterministic paths, such as"Find iPhone 15."Real shopping scenarios are inherently more layered, involving multi-dimensional product attributes, search filters, and user-specific sorting preferences. items.abstract_600: Learning on Graphs has attracted immense attention due to its wide real-world applications. items.title: LLM4Rerank: LLM-based Auto-Reranking Framework for Recommendations
items.abstract_600: Reranking is significant for recommender systems due to its pivotal role in refining recommendation results. Numerous reranking models have emerged to meet diverse reranking requirements in practical applications, which not only prioritize accuracy but also consider additional aspects such as diversity and fairness.
